newsitem.title: GERMANY: German chemical industry upbeat for full yr 97.
newsitem.headline: German chemical industry upbeat for full yr 97.

text.p: The German chemical industry's recovery continued in early 1997, leaving firms confident the full year will show stronger results, industry association VCI said on Tuesday.
The association said that production rose by an average 7.5 percent in both January and February from year-earlier levels.
Exports were largely responsible for the increase as the global economic recovery continued, VCI said in a statement.
The group said a decline in the mark's value helped make German products cheaper abroad, contributing to buoyant international demand.
Heartened by results in the first two months where firms had called the business climate satisfactory, the mood brightened further.
The majority of firms polled by the Munich-based Ifo institute said they expected more positive signs, adding the favourable outlook for exports largely shaped their opinions.
VCI predicted that during the year as a whole, chemical production would expand markedly, although the growth rate is expected to be below those seen in the first two months.
The industry was also able to uphold promises made in last year's wage contract to continue training workers, marking some sort of job security. -- Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525
